### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/src/index.ts`, `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-rename-planner.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/deployment/install-modes.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in start), targetNamespace (literal, a string literal in targetNamespaceOf))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in start))_

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via INVALID_REQUEST (literal, a string literal in start))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/src/index.ts`, `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-rename-planner.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aad7d2f2df5787e45634e018686c8f93c8a4d185` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6a1c4a4d86333e509ca8ed6fe61fbfdb1257c570` — the merge of head `88c0a71cadda0bf2cdf8449dc927e0ecdb456c5f` into base `aad7d2f2df5787e45634e018686c8f93c8a4d185`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6a1c4a4d86333e509ca8ed6fe61fbfdb1257c570 && git checkout 6a1c4a4d86333e509ca8ed6fe61fbfdb1257c570
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin aad7d2f2df5787e45634e018686c8f93c8a4d185 88c0a71cadda0bf2cdf8449dc927e0ecdb456c5f && git checkout -B drift-repro aad7d2f2df5787e45634e018686c8f93c8a4d185 && git merge --no-ff 88c0a71cadda0bf2cdf8449dc927e0ecdb456c5f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aad7d2f2df5787e45634e018686c8f93c8a4d185
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs aad7d2f2df5787e45634e018686c8f93c8a4d185` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c48adec9e7c7bf99616879a8e6455744463919bf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/index.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/install-local-door-service.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-grant-refusal-audit.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-rename-planner.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/MarketplacePackagePage.tsx + packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts (`ManifestSchema.shape.namespace`), packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts (`ImportUnmanagedPackageRequestSchema.targetNamespace`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/marketplaceApi.ts (the Console's hosted sender), all read only

Inputs: card #31482 body and its 8 comments, the PR body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...c48adec9e` (9 files, +283 / -21), the check-runs on the head. The seat thread's "rulings 1 to 6" are not on the card and were not read.

Check-runs on the head: no failure. Completed and green: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Build UI Deps, Check PR Size. Still in progress when this record was written, so their gate verdicts are not in: Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 9/16 (10/16 to 16/16 not yet listed), Lint · ESLint, Lint UI, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, the three Lint · scoped runs, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · source gates. This verdict judges the contract; it does not stand in for those runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- `POST /api/v1/cloud-connection/install`, `target_namespace` beside `install_mode: 'unmanaged'`: newly read, parsed by `ManifestSchema.shape.namespace` by reference, sent as `params.target_namespace`. A widening. Right.
- The same key beside a managed install or no mode: ignored on main, now `400 INVALID_REQUEST` before the control plane is asked. A narrowing, declared. Right. `null` is read as absent on the route, so `target_namespace: null` beside managed still installs; the door refuses its own `null` there. Harmless difference.
- A malformed value beside unmanaged: ignored on main, now 400 with `details.targetNamespace`. A second narrowing, covered by the same declaration. Right.
- Asked, and the grant echoes none or another: copied into the source namespace on main (the key was ignored), now `502 PLUGIN_INSTALL_FAILED`, nothing copied, audited. Right, fail closed.
- A non-string `data.target_namespace` on a grant, asked or not: copied on main, now 502. Right.
- No ask, the grant names a string: the copy now takes that namespace where main kept the source's. A behaviour change driven by the control plane alone. Stated in the changeset. Right, on the "grant governs" design; see ③.
- No ask, no echo: unchanged, and the request sent to the control plane is byte-for-byte main's. Pinned by two CONTROL tests. Right.
- New export `TARGET_NAMESPACE_ON_MANAGED_INSTALL_MESSAGE` in `install-local-door-service.ts`. That file is not re-exported from `index.ts`, so the package's public surface does not move. The door's step 0″ text is unchanged in the diff (same three string pieces). Right.
- `index.ts`, `marketplace-install-rename-planner.ts`, `MarketplacePackagePage.tsx`: comments only. No accept-set change.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/cloud-connection` is right: the change is not a metadata-protocol change (`Metadata-protocol: none` holds, no authorable key moves), and AGENTS.md ships a non-protocol change at `patch`, breaking or not, with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The changeset carries the banner, the fix for a refused request (drop the key, or send `install_mode: 'unmanaged'`), one `adr-0087: not-required` marker, and both declaration lines. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset matches the diff: a yes for the new key, the narrowing arm for the managed refusal. Check Changeset and the PR-body guards are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_question 1 (`details.targetNamespace` at the route while the wire key is `target_namespace`): option A is accepted. One details key across the route, the door and the import is what a re-asking dialog needs. The mixed spelling it leaves on this route is finding S1 below.
- open_question 2 (an unasked, malformed echo answers the import's 400 rather than 502): option A accepted for now. Nothing is copied and the 400 names the value. Carry option B on the follow-up card.
- Dev flag, cross-repo NOT MEASURED: the spelling `params.target_namespace` in and `data.target_namespace` echoed is not confirmed anywhere on the card. The card's newest words on it say the opposite direction: 6721710740 "don't forward it to cloud" and 6722704329 "not on the forward to cloud". The PR cites seat rulings 1 to 6 that are not on the card. Escalated as finding S2.
- Card task "fix the `30963-hosted-install-mode.md` prose": not done. The pending changeset still says "a cloud base, no install-local door" and will ship in the CHANGELOG. The PR cites seat ruling 5, also off the card. Part of S2.
- Item 3 (the install dialog) split to a `domain:ui` follow-up card: within the card's own allowance (6754591423). The consumer note 6754798360 expects the conflict as `400 INVALID_REQUEST details.targetNamespace`; the tree answers an owned namespace with `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT details { namespace, owners }`. The follow-up card and cloud must be told; the PR's pin is right about the tree.
- Deviations (stale `origin/main` on the first gate round, worker restart, ablations at 8a9db617e before the merge, app-shell tests left to CI): none touches the contract. Type Check UI and Test UI are among the runs still in progress.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing holds. The published spec on `main` declares `targetNamespace` only on the unmanaged copy (`ImportUnmanagedPackageRequestSchema`), and the install-local door already refuses it beside a managed install (step 0″, #30794). The hosted route declared no such key on `main`; it ignored it. So nothing declared is taken away at the consumer: the route now gives the refusal the door already gives. The Console's hosted sender (`marketplaceApi.ts`) sends `package_id`, `seed_sample_data` and `install_mode` only, so no first-party request is refused.

Tried to break it:
- Managed refusal ordering: it runs before the value is judged and before any fetch. Holds.
- `ManifestSchema.shape.namespace` is `.optional()`, but `undefined` and `null` are returned before the parse, so no value slips through as "absent". Holds.
- The grant check: the version reasons win over the namespace reason, and the "may have installed managed" note only appears when `install_mode` was not echoed, so a namespace 502 never carries it. Holds.
- A forged body namespace cannot reach the door: only `data.target_namespace` is handed over. Holds, pinned.
- An empty-string echo with no ask reaches the door as `targetNamespace: ''` and is judged there. Fail closed.

Findings:

- **S1, should-fix.** The route reads `packageId`, `installMode` and `seedSampleData` in camelCase beside their snake spellings, but `target_namespace` in snake only, and it ignores a camelCase `targetNamespace`. The refusal sentence the route now answers teaches exactly the camelCase pair (`installMode: 'unmanaged'`, `targetNamespace`). A caller who follows it and sends `{ installMode: 'unmanaged', targetNamespace: 'acme' }` gets a 200 and a copy in the source namespace (or the control plane's default), which the changeset itself calls "not what was asked"; beside a managed install the same key is still silently ignored, the behaviour this PR sets out to end. The test "a `targetNamespace` in the caller's body never reaches the door" pins the silence. Fix one way: refuse a non-null `targetNamespace` on this route with a 400 that names `target_namespace`, or read it as the second spelling the way `installModeOf` does (disagreement refused). Either moves the head and widens the declared narrowing, so restate the changeset with it.
- **S2, should-fix (record, no head move).** Put on the card, before merge: the ruling that the grant governs the namespace and that the route forwards `params.target_namespace` (it reverses 6721710740 and 6722704329 as written), cloud's confirmation that PR #4206 reads that param and echoes `data.target_namespace`, and the ruling that leaves the stale 30963 changeset as written. Without the echo, every install that names a namespace answers 502 after the control plane has recorded its grant; that is fail closed and stated, but the card must show the maintainer chose it.
- **N1, nit.** On the namespace 502 the audit event carries no namespace, so the environment's row does not say which name was asked or echoed. Follow-up at most.
- **N2, nit.** `target_namespace` is not trimmed while `version` is; a padded value answers 400 from the pattern. Consistent with the declaration, no action.

No must-fix. S1 and S2 each earn a delta review of their fix.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `88c0a71ca` (fix commit da14ba028, then a merge of `main` at 09bf7de71)
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/install-local-door-service.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/package-lifecycle-audit.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/package-lifecycle-audit.test.ts, .changeset/31482-unmanaged-grant-target-namespace.md. None of the 8 commits merged in from `main` touches this PR's files. Every other path is unchanged since c48adec9.

This is a delta review of record 6756998867 (head c48adec9). That record was a PASS with one should-fix (S1) and two nits (N1, N2); the seat's rulings are at 6757010844. This head adds one fix commit and one merge of `main`. The PR body is patched to r3 by the seat and read back as identical.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **S1 is closed.** `targetNamespaceOf` reads `target_namespace` and `targetNamespace` the way `installModeOf` reads its two spellings. If both are sent with different values, the answer is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` naming both, and nothing is sent to the control plane. That check runs before the managed-install refusal and before the value is parsed. Either spelling beside a managed install, or with no `install_mode`, is refused `400` with the door's sentence. Three new pins cover this:
   - camel is forwarded;
   - camel beside a managed install is refused;
   - the two spellings in conflict give 400.

   One pin from the first head ("a caller-body `targetNamespace` never reaches the door") was replaced, because camel is now an ask. The replacement pins that a camel ask the grant does not echo still answers 502 with no door call. The grant still governs. No test from `main` was edited.
2. **The accept set moves by one more refusal:** two spellings that disagree. It is declared in the changeset's `Clause-②` line and its BREAKING paragraph. No first-party caller sends either key, so nothing moves for them. This is right.
3. **N2 is closed.** A string is trimmed before `ManifestSchema.shape.namespace` judges it, as `version` already is. The comparison of the two spellings happens before the trim, so `" crm"` beside `"crm"` is a 400 conflict and not a silent pick. That is the stricter reading, and I accept it.
4. **N1 is closed.** The 502 for a grant refused over its namespace (and only when the version was read) audits `requestedNamespace`, plus `grantedNamespace` when the grant named one. `plugin-audit` writes them on that row only, as metadata `requested_namespace` / `granted_namespace` (`null` when absent). Both keys are optional on both event types, so every other row is unchanged. Pinned in plugin-audit.
5. **Ablations (thread report):** A5 to A9 each turned red and were restored, with `git diff HEAD` empty afterwards. On base, 11 of the 15 pins fail; the 4 that pass are the two CONTROLs and the two door pins.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, and now also on `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, which gains two optional metadata keys on one row. This is right.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is restated to cover both spellings and the conflict.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- The ADR-0087 marker is unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Cloud's confirmation of the #4206 shape** is not a landing gate (seat ruling). On landing, the seat tells cloud mailbox #31366 (cloud#3648 item 4).
- **#32040** (the UI dialog follow-up) is linked from the body.
- **Gates (thread report):**
  - cloud-connection: 80 files, 1178 tests.
  - plugin-audit: 81 files, 1260 tests.
  - Typecheck and lint exit 0.
  - 79 derived gates, all exit 0, none NOT-MEASURED.
  - Full dogfood: 3690 passed, 42 skipped.

### ④ Design judgment

No new finding.

Check-runs on this head were still running when this record was written. Landing waits for them to finish all green.
